what: Where the work has gone, and what has come back. One row per outward send, with the status word meant exactly. This is a RECORD, not prose: the About page renders it, so updating a status is a record edit and the page cannot quietly go stale.

statusWords.public, no reply: visible to everyone, answered by nobody
statusWords.filed, no reply: received by the other party's tracker, unanswered
statusWords.posted, no reply: published where it was aimed, unanswered
statusWords.open, no comments: an issue nobody has responded to
statusWords.live, no reply: a comment visible in the thread, unanswered
statusWords.posted, visibility unconfirmed: submitted, and we have not verified it appeared
statusWords.submitted, awaiting moderation: in a queue, not yet visible
statusWords.still in the moderation queue: submitted and confirmed not yet visible

rows.what: A correction to a GPT-published constant on Erdős #852 — refuted at its 12th significant digit, certified replacement attached.
rows.where: the problem's discussion thread on erdosproblems.com
rows.note: It cleared moderation and stands visible. The thread as it stands is pinned in this repository as evidence bytes. Visible is not endorsed: nobody has answered it, no author has amended anything, and clearing a moderation queue is not peer review and not an independent rerun.

rows.what: An independent confirmation of the computational appendix of a claimed proof of Erdős #1038 — all 30 printed decimals verified by a different route, Krawczyk rather than bisection.
rows.where: an issue on the claiming authors' own repository
rows.note: To my knowledge still the only independent verification of any part of any of the three claimed proofs of that problem.

rows.what: An evaluation note on a public automated-alignment sandbox whose authors invited stress-testing.
A note on Erdős #290, whose constant's decimal expansion is also an OEIS submission.
The Erdős #290 square-discriminant law as exact integer identities, with a certified bracket for the Galois-density constant — and a correction to my own earlier write-up, in the same comment.
rows.note: Superseded on the mathematics five days later by arXiv:2609.00104, which proves the liminf exactly; our bracket is now the certified numeric value of that constant rather than one end of a range, and the page says so. A follow-up comment is written and unsent.

rows.what: Both ends of Erdős #1038: per-degree theorems on the supremum side, then a certified lower bound inf ≥ 1.828 with no tail estimate and no assumed minimizer.
rows.note: The second comment was edited after posting to fix rendering: GitHub's KaTeX rejects \\operatorname and renders \\, as a visible comma.

rows.what: λ(4) = −L(1,2,3,4) offered as an unusually clean Lean formalization target — six elementary lemmas, exact rational identities, and 2,231 finite cases each carrying a certified enclosure.
The same infimum result, rewritten for the forum's own rules — derivations pushed to the linked PDF because the site forbids posting partial proofs in full.
rows.note: The site queues comments for moderation and I have not confirmed this one visible.

rows.what: A note on Chowla's cosine problem (#510) and the λ(4) result.
rows.note: Checked by tools/sweep-claims.js, which watches for it appearing.

rows.what: A request to the authors of the 604-point dimension-11 kissing configuration for their vectors, so the one NEEDS DATA row in our ledger can be decided.
rows.note: The ask is offer-shaped: the certification is already built and waiting on the bytes.
